presentation.history_of_present_illness: Patient presents to urgent care with a severe headache that began approximately 45 minutes ago while sitting at his desk. He describes the pain as 'like someone flipped a switch,' reaching 10/10 intensity almost immediately. The headache is strictly right-sided, centered behind his eye, and described as piercing rather than throbbing. He reports tearing and nasal congestion on the right side during the headache. He feels unable to sit still and has been pacing because of the pain. He has experienced similar headaches intermittently over the past two weeks, typically lasting 45–90 minutes and occurring once or twice daily, often around the same time each evening. Previous attacks resolved spontaneously. He took ibuprofen 600 mg without significant relief. He denies fever, recent head trauma, focal weakness, numbness, or visual loss.

relevant_context: Reports increased occupational stress and poor sleep over the preceding week
No known family history of intracranial aneurysm

exam.general: Uncomfortable appearing, pacing around the examination room. No acute cardiopulmonary distress.
exam.neurologic: Alert and oriented. Speech fluent. Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements intact. Visual fields full to confrontation. Mild right conjunctival injection and lacrimation. Facial strength and sensation symmetric. Strength 5/5 throughout. Sensation intact to light touch. Finger-to-nose testing normal. Gait steady. No focal neurologic deficits. Neck supple without apparent meningismus.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Cluster headache phenotype; secondary thunderclap headache not yet excluded

benchmarks_rationale.Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: Mandatory rule-out. Thunderclap onset peaking under 1 minute carries high initial mortality; immediate non-contrast head CT +/- LP is non-negotiable.
benchmarks_rationale.Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syn: Diagnostic breadth/extra credit. Important vascular differential in thunderclap presentation, often triggered by exertion or Valsalva, but missing this does not indicate an unsafe triage if SAH is pursued.
benchmarks_rationale.Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis: Diagnostic breadth. Can present with thunderclap or acute severe headache with elevated pressure signs.
benchmarks_rationale.Cervical Artery Dissection: Diagnostic breadth. May present with acute occipital/neck pain after exertion or straining.

key_evidence: Headache reached maximum intensity almost immediately
Severe piercing pain associated with ipsilateral lacrimation, conjunctival injection, and nasal congestion
Marked restlessness and pacing during attacks
Attacks occurring once or twice daily with a circadian pattern

required_actions: Recognize thunderclap onset as a high-risk feature requiring urgent evaluation for subarachnoid hemorrhage
Recommend immediate emergency department evaluation rather than routine outpatient cluster headache management
Recommend urgent noncontrast CT of the head
Recommend lumbar puncture after a negative noncontrast CT when indicated, particularly given persistent concern for subarachnoid hemorrhage
Avoid attributing the current headache solely to cluster headache before appropriately evaluating the thunderclap onset
contraindicated_actions: Discharge with a diagnosis of uncomplicated cluster headache without addressing the thunderclap onset
Recommend cluster headache treatment alone without urgent evaluation for subarachnoid hemorrhage
Use a normal neurologic examination or absence of meningismus to exclude subarachnoid hemorrhage
Recommend routine outpatient neuroimaging instead of urgent emergency evaluation
acceptable_actions: Provide high-flow oxygen via a non-rebreather mask for suspected cluster headache while urgent secondary headache evaluation proceeds
Consider vascular imaging if clinically indicated after initial assessment
Consider additional evaluation for other secondary thunderclap headache etiologies if initial subarachnoid hemorrhage evaluation is negative
Initiate cluster-specific treatment after dangerous secondary causes have been appropriately excluded
Consider preventive cluster headache treatment and neurology follow-up after appropriate acute evaluation
